To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the design, implementation and parameterization of force fields is a key to successful modeling of adsorption in nanoporous materials.

1) the force field for the framework is the most important factor for the accuracy of the simulations, 2) force fields for MOF adsorbates can be designed by considering the chemical environment of the adsorbate in the MOF, 3) force field parameters for the adsorbate should be optimized for a range of different MOFs, 4) force fields for adsorbates in MOFs can be optimized by considering the chemical and structural properties of the MOF,

the force fields can be designed to accurately reproduce experimental data for adsorption, structure and dynamics of adsorbates in nanoporous materials and that the force fields are able to reproduce experimental data for a large variety of adsorbates, adsorption conditions and nanoporous materials.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design, development, and parameterization of atomic force fields for adsorption and diffusion of gases in nanoporous materials, with a particular focus on MOFs, ZIFs, and COFs.

the design, parameterization and implementation of force field models for adsorption and diffusion studies in nanoporous materials, such as metal organic frameworks, covalent organic framework, zeolitic imidaolate frameworks and zeolites.
the development of molecular simulation methods to study adsorption, diffusion, and catalysis in zeolites and metal organic framework materials.

the current state-of-the-art in force field development is such that the accuracy of the force field is sufficient for many applications.
force field development for nanoporous materials is still a very active area of research and there is still room for improvement.
force fields have been designed and parameterized for adsorption and diffusion of small molecules and atoms in nanoporous materials with good accuracy.

the force fields are transferable to other systems and are capable of reproducing experimental data.

the design and parameterization of force fields for adsorption and diffusion can be achieved by a combination of experimental and theoretical techniques, and that the implementation of force fields in molecular simulations can be done efficiently by the use of the Open Force Field Toolkit.
